# Known finding-set diffs between guff and golangci-lint (R21).
# Format: <target> <guff-only|golangci-only> <normalized-key>
# normalized-key = relpath:line:linter:message
# Regenerated by: ./compat/run.sh --update-allowlist
#
# Prefer fixing guff over growing this list. Entries here are accepted
# mismatches (message phrasing, enable-set gaps, known DEFERRED).
#
# WARNING: `--update-allowlist` rewrites this file from the current diff and
# drops the comments below. The rationale for every entry is kept in
# docs/COMPAT-HARDENING.md §5, which is the copy to read and to update.
#
# Keys are pinned to jaeger v2.20.0 (corpus/hunt.json), so the line numbers are
# stable until that ref moves.
#
# revive ×2 — `time-naming` and `epoch-naming`, both true positives that guff
# reports and golangci-lint 2.12.2 does not. This is §6's standing decision
# ("do not follow revive's importer blindness"), and it is the *whole* of the
# jaeger diff.
#
# Measured 2026-08-31 (docs/COMPAT-HARDENING.md §4, 続き 106), thirteen shapes
# in a scratch module with only these two rules enabled. guff, revive v1.15.0
# run standalone, and golangci-lint 2.12.2 run with GOROOT exported all produce
# the *same eight* findings and stay silent on the same five (alias of
# time.Duration, a same-package named type, no unit suffix, `:=` instead of a
# ValueSpec, a correct suffix). golangci-lint as installed produces none of
# them.
#
# The reason is not in revive's rules and not in guff. revive type-checks its
# own files with `types.Config{Importer: importer.Default()}` (lint/package.go
# TypeCheck), and since Go 1.20 that importer reaches stdlib export data by
# running `$build.Default.GOROOT/bin/go list -export`
# (internal/exportdata.lookupGorootExport). golangci-lint means to point
# build.Default.GOROOT at the real toolchain — pkg/lint/package.go
# prepareBuildContext does exactly that — but it reads the value through
# `func (e Env) Discover(...)` (pkg/goutil/env.go), a **value receiver** that
# assigns the discovered map to its own copy, so `Env.Get(GOROOT)` returns "".
# prepareBuildContext then returns early and build.Default.GOROOT keeps the
# GOROOT baked into the binary at *its* build time. This host's golangci-lint is
# the Homebrew build: go1.26.2, GOROOT /opt/homebrew/Cellar/go/1.26.2/libexec,
# a directory Homebrew deleted when Go moved to 1.26.4/1.26.5. Every import in
# every package therefore fails, `time.Duration` is invalid, and all thirteen
# type-dependent revive rules report nothing.
#
# So upstream's silence here is a property of *where the golangci-lint binary
# was compiled versus where Go lives on the measuring host*, not of its source.
# Exporting GOROOT (honoured: Env.Get reads os.Getenv first) makes upstream
# agree with guff on all thirteen shapes, and on both jaeger lines:
#
#   $ GOROOT="$(go env GOROOT)" ./compat/hunt.sh --name jaeger
#     jaeger: guff=2 golangci=89 both=2       <- the two below become `both`
#
# The harness deliberately does *not* export it: every golden, allowlist and
# baseline in this repository is calibrated against the blind importer, and
# `unhandled-error` is ported to match it on purpose (crates/guff-revive/src/
# rules/unhandled_error.rs `callee_is_local`). That same run shows what the
# recalibration would cost — 87 golangci-only `unhandled-error` findings on
# stdlib calls (`fmt.Println`, `io.Writer.Write`, `os.Process.Wait`) that guff
# suppresses. Non-stdlib imports stay invisible to `importer.Default()` even
# with GOROOT set, so the boundary would become "same package or stdlib", not
# "everything". That is a separate decision, recorded in §6.
jaeger guff-only cmd/jaeger/internal/extension/jaegerquery/internal/mcptools/internal/handlers/search_traces.go:141:revive:time-naming: var durationMin is of type time.Duration; don't use unit-specific suffix "Min"
jaeger guff-only internal/storage/v2/cassandra/tracestore/from_dbmodel_test.go:27:revive:epoch-naming: var testSpanEventTime should have one of these suffixes: Micro, Microsecond, Microseconds, Us
